ai.description: This medium-sized frog reaches 40–45 mm. It is brown with dark mottling and a pale venter. Distinctive features include prominent nuptial spines on the male's chest and expanded, truncate digit tips.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops kohimaensis* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, small, blackish-brown spinules on the dorsal skin, which are absent in most similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Amolops kohimaensis* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within subtropical broadleaf forests at elevations ranging from approximately 1,400 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Amolops kohimaensis* is primarily nocturnal, utilizing its specialized adhesive toe pads to forage for insects along the slippery, fast-flowing rocks of mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops kohimaensis* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying clutches of approximately 150–200 eggs on submerged rocks in streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops kohimaensis* is endemic to the state of Nagaland in Northeast India, where it inhabits high-altitude mountain streams within the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.callDescription: The Kohima Spiny Torrent Frog produces a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing mountain streams in its rocky habitat.
